desc: CESNET libyang through 6.4.13 contains an incomplete cleanup vulnerability in ly_out_reset() in src/out.c that tests a stale errno ESPIPE value after a successful seek. title: POCO C++ Libraries through 1.15.4 contain a denial of service vulnerability in InflatingStreamBuf::reset() and InflatingInputStream::reset() that fails to discard unconsumed…
desc: POCO C++ Libraries through 1.15.4 contain a denial of service vulnerability in InflatingStreamBuf::reset() and InflatingInputStream::reset() that fails to discard unconsumed compressed input after decompression errors. Attackers can supply one corrupt zlib, gzip or zip-deflate stream to applications reusing an InflatingInputStream, causing all later stream reads, including valid ones, to fail.

desc: Open Babel through 3.2.1 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in OBForceField::Setup() that leaves stored constraints bound to freed atoms when set up with an empty molecule. Attackers can supply a molecule file yielding an empty molecule so later SteepestDescent() or ConjugateGradients() calls read freed memory, causing crashes or incorrect results.

title: In the `setup-osc` GitHub Action of Eclipse Apoapsis, from commit 4e9eaff up to, but not including, commit 03efc4c, the ORT Server version returned by the `/api/v1/versions`…
desc:
In the `setup-osc` GitHub Action of Eclipse Apoapsis, from commit 4e9eaff up to, but not including, commit 03efc4c, the ORT Server version returned by the `/api/v1/versions` endpoint is inserted into a shell script via a GitHub Actions expression without validation. An attacker who controls the responses of the configured ORT Server, for example by compromising the server, can execute arbitrary commands on the GitHub Actions runner and access the secrets available to the calling workflow.



The issue is fixed in commit 03efc4c, which only accepts version strings consisting of alphanumeric characters, `.`, `+`, and `-`.

title: In Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server versions 0.1.0 to 0.83.0, the file-based configuration providers do not restrict resolved file paths to the configured directory.
desc:
In Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server versions 0.1.0 to 0.83.0, the file-based configuration providers do not restrict resolved file paths to the configured directory. An authenticated user who is allowed to trigger an ORT run for a single repository can use `../` sequences or absolute paths in `reporter-template://` references of the reporter job configuration to make the reporter worker read arbitrary files and include them in the generated reports. This discloses files such as environment variables, mounted secrets, and configuration files that contain credentials shared across all tenants of the server.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server 0.84.0.

title: In Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server Credential Helper versions 0.1.0 to 0.2.0, as shipped with Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server versions 0.65.0 to 0.83.0, the Git credential helper selects…
desc:
In Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server Credential Helper versions 0.1.0 to 0.2.0, as shipped with Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server versions 0.65.0 to 0.83.0, the Git credential helper selects stored credentials by re-parsing the requested URL with a regular expression that can be confused by `:` and `@` characters in the URL path. An attacker who can make an ORT Server worker fetch a crafted Git URL, for example through a submodule of a repository that is analyzed, can obtain credentials stored for a different host, such as `github.com`, which Git then sends to the attacker-controlled server.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server Credential Helper 0.2.1 and Eclipse Apoapsis ORT Server 0.84.0.

title: A flaw was found in the Admin REST API v2 of Keycloak.
desc: A flaw was found in the Admin REST API v2 of Keycloak. This component is used by administrators to manage realm configurations, including clients. By sending a request with a mismatched client ID in the body, an authenticated user without any administrative privileges can distinguish between existing and non-existing clients based on whether the server returns a 400 Bad Request or a 403 Forbidden error.

title: Pydantic AI Harness's PlaywrightBrowser enforces its egress policy on HTTP requests and page WebSockets, but not on WebRTC or WebTransport connections, WebSockets opened with…
desc:
Pydantic AI Harness's PlaywrightBrowser enforces its egress policy on HTTP requests and page WebSockets, but not on WebRTC or WebTransport connections, WebSockets opened with WebSocketStream, or the requests the browser itself sends for FedCM. A page the agent opens can make the browser send WebRTC (STUN and TURN), WebTransport and WebSocketStream traffic, and FedCM requests, to hosts and ports that the policy refuses, including under a policy that limits every request kind to an allowlist.

This affects applications that use PlaywrightBrowser to open pages an attacker can influence. The traffic is each protocol's connection setup, sent to a destination the page chooses. A page can learn whether a target answers a STUN request. No response body from an ordinary internal service was readable through WebRTC, WebTransport or FedCM. A WebSocketStream is an ordinary WebSocket that the WebSocket guard does not see, opened from a page, a frame or a worker, and the page reads what the server sends, including from a private address. Chromium's Local Network Access blocks WebTransport from public pages to private addresses, but does not block WebRTC.

A FedCM call (navigator.credentials.get with an identity provider) makes the browser fetch the provider's /.well-known/web-identity, config, accounts and client metadata URLs. The page chooses the config URL's path and the client ID, so it can send data to a host outside allowed_domains or listed in blocked_domains. The accounts request carries the provider's cookies from the browser profile. FedCM requires a provider origin that is HTTPS or loopback.

The assumed attacker is a third party with no access to the application who controls script on a page the agent opens.

Under an enforced egress policy, which is the default, pydantic-ai-harness 0.74.0 removes RTCPeerConnection, webkitRTCPeerConnection, WebTransport, WebSocketStream, IdentityCredential and IdentityProvider from every page and frame, refuses FedCM calls to navigator.credentials.get, and launches Chromium with FedCM and WebSocketStream turned off. These paths stay outside the policy: WebTransport from workers; WebSocketStream from workers in a browser reached over cdp_url; WebTransport in sandboxed iframes that Chromium runs in their own process (headless=False and cdp_url); and documents loaded before attachment under cdp_context='default'.

Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.74.0 or later. For the paths the upgrade leaves open, and until you upgrade, run the browser behind a network egress filter that also covers UDP, or do not open untrusted URLs with PlaywrightBrowser.

title: OpenProject 17.2.0 before 17.5.2, 17.6.0 before 17.6.1, 17.7.0 before 17.7.3, 17.8.0 before 17.8.2, and 17.9.0 before 17.9.7 contains an externally controlled method selection…
desc: OpenProject 17.2.0 before 17.5.2, 17.6.0 before 17.6.1, 17.7.0 before 17.7.3, 17.8.0 before 17.8.2, and 17.9.0 before 17.9.7 contains an externally controlled method selection vulnerability in InplaceEditFieldsController via the unvalidated attribute parameter. desc: SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a reachable assertion in RTCP decoding that lets remote WebRTC peers crash the server. title: SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in SrsRtcpCommon::decode and SrsRtcpTWCC::decode that lets remote…

desc: ai-memory 2.6.0 before 3.3.2 contains a symlink following vulnerability in the ai-memory-wikisync companion that allows local attackers to overwrite arbitrary files by planting symlinks at predictable temporary names. title: COVESA Open1722 before 0.9.8 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Avtp_Vss_CalcVssPathLength in src/avtp/acf/custom/Vss.c, which reads the INTEROP path-length prefix…
desc: COVESA Open1722 before 0.9.8 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Avtp_Vss_CalcVssPathLength in src/avtp/acf/custom/Vss.c, which reads the INTEROP path-length prefix without checking the declared ACF message length. desc: league/commonmark 2.6.0 before 2.10.8 contains a denial of service vulnerability in DelimiterStack::push() that miscounts delimiter runs against the max_delimiters_per_line budget. title: GNU Inetutils talkd Stack-based Buffer Overflow Denial-of-Service Vulnerability.
desc:
GNU Inetutils talkd Stack-based Buffer Overflow Denial-of-Service Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create a denial-of-service condition on affected installations of GNU Inetutils. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the processing of announce requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create a denial-of-service condition on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-29120.

title: GNU Inetutils FTP Client File Retrieval Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability.
desc:
GNU Inetutils FTP Client File Retrieval Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of GNU Inetutils FTP Client. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must interact with a malicious FTP server.

The specific flaw exists within the processing of filenames. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current user. Was ZDI-CAN-29119.

title: psqlODBC rewrites statement text for keyset-driven cursors and ODBC escapes using positions it found in the text.
desc:
psqlODBC rewrites statement text for keyset-driven cursors and ODBC escapes using positions it found in the text. These positions could lie outside the text or describe another statement:

- After SQLExecDirect() failed on a statement handle, the FROM and WHERE positions of the failed statement were applied to the next, shorter statement on that handle.
- The parser could record a FROM position with no text after it, and the rewrite then copied a negative length.
- An {fn …} escape whose arguments contain FOR UPDATE, ; or INTO … FROM made the driver remove a cursor prefix from the wrong buffer.
- {fn CONVERT(?, …)} with an output parameter produced a negative argument length.
- An unclosed {fn …} escape made the driver read past the statement, and a few thousand nested ones exhausted the stack.
- Translating @@identity in long statement text read an uninitialised pointer, and {? = call …} with nothing bound for the return value dereferenced NULL.

Whoever supplies the text of a statement that an application opens on a keyset-driven or dynamic cursor with a concurrency other than read-only, or calls with an output parameter, can corrupt the application's heap and end it. That includes the users of query tools, report builders and other applications that run SQL their users type. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: psqlODBC assumed that a table it reads keeps the definition it had when the statement was described or parsed.
desc:
psqlODBC assumed that a table it reads keeps the definition it had when the statement was described or parsed. A database user who owns a table or view another user's application reads can crash that application, with an honest server and default options, in these cases:

- Columns dropped or added in another session while the application updates rows through an updatable cursor, or describes the columns with Parse=1.
- A view whose ctid is NULL, read through an updatable cursor, which writes past the row cache, and a view with a volatile filter scrolled backward with UseDeclareFetch=1.
- Rows added through an updatable cursor to a table with child tables or partitions.
- A column whose type is named lo, written with data-at-execution parameters.
- A DROP TABLE or ALTER TABLE on the connection while another statement still uses the table's column information.
- NULL key columns in rows the driver re-reads for an updatable cursor.
- A function called with more output parameters than its result has columns.
- SQLTables() and SQLTablesW() dereferenced NULL when called with empty strings for the catalog, schema and table names together with a NULL TableType, which kills the process that loaded the driver and every session it serves.

The demonstrated results are crashes; one case writes past a heap buffer, but code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: When Debug or CommLog is enabled and the log directory cannot be used, psqlODBC falls back to a directory under the user's home directory.
desc:
When Debug or CommLog is enabled and the log directory cannot be used, psqlODBC falls back to a directory under the user's home directory. It wrote that path with an unexpanded ~, which is resolved relative to the process's current directory. Another local user who controls a directory on that path can make the driver create the victim's mylog_*.log and psqlodbc_*.log files in any directory the victim can write to, or leave the victim's process blocked in open().

This completes the fix for CVE-2026-120066 in 18.00.0006.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: With SQL_C_DEFAULT, the C type of a bound column or parameter follows its SQL type.
desc:
With SQL_C_DEFAULT, the C type of a bound column or parameter follows its SQL type. An application sizes its buffer from the type it was told when it described the statement. When the column had another type at fetch time, because the server reported another type, the table was altered, or an output parameter's result column had another type, psqlODBC wrote the larger type into the smaller buffer: 12 bytes past a 4-byte buffer for a uuid, and more in multi-row fetches, where the driver also steps through the array by the larger size.

Other conversions wrote past the application's buffer as well:

- With Int8As set to a smaller type, an int8 column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT was still written as 8 bytes.
- An int2vector column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT returned unterminated binary data instead of text.
- An output parameter that the application discards by binding a NULL buffer overflowed a stack buffer in the driver.
- SQLGetData() with BufferLength 0 on a column the driver reads as a large object wrote a NUL byte past the buffer.
- Adding a row with SQLBulkOperations(SQL_ADD) on a static updatable cursor before the first fetch, then changing that row, rolling back and fetching it, made the keyset index arithmetic free a pointer that was never allocated and corrupt the heap.

This can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable), and by the owner of a table the application reads.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: psqlODBC mapped an SSLmode value in a connection string that it did not recognise, such as SSLmode=Require, SSLmode=Verify-Full, SSLmode={require} or SSLmode={verify-full}, to…
desc:
psqlODBC mapped an SSLmode value in a connection string that it did not recognise, such as SSLmode=Require, SSLmode=Verify-Full, SSLmode={require} or SSLmode={verify-full}, to disable. SQLDriverConnect() then returned SQL_SUCCESS with no diagnostic, and the connection was not encrypted.

An attacker on the network path of such a connection can read and change its traffic.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: A parameter-array execution that fails part-way leaves the rows it has already queued on the statement handle, and the next execution on that handle sends them.
desc:
A parameter-array execution that fails part-way leaves the rows it has already
queued on the statement handle, and the next execution on that handle sends
them. After a data-at-execution batch is abandoned, by SQLCancel or a
rejected SQLPutData, the next SQLExecDirect sends the failed batch's rows
and returns SQL_SUCCESS without sending its own statement.

So an application that logs the failure on the same handle has its log entry
turned into a silent no-op, while rows it was told had failed are stored. An
end user who controls one value in an application's array insert can arrange
both halves of that.

A second route needs no data-at-execution parameter: when building a later row
fails in parameter conversion, the queued rows go to the server ahead of the
next parameter array on the handle, inside whatever transaction and session
settings are current by then. One variant also writes past the end of a shorter
SQL_ATTR_PARAM_STATUS_PTR array supplied by the next statement.

The statements that run are the application's own, correctly quoted; no SQL
text comes from outside.

Versions from psqlODBC 12.02.0000, which introduced batched parameter-array
execution, up to and including 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: psqlODBC did not check that a server reply matches the query it sent: that a FETCH returns no more rows than it asked for, that each row has the described number of columns, that…
desc:
psqlODBC did not check that a server reply matches the query it sent: that a FETCH returns no more rows than it asked for, that each row has the described number of columns, that one query produces one result, and that a COPY, a transaction or the connection ends where the protocol says. By sending replies that do not match, a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable) can corrupt memory in the application:

- A FETCH reply with more rows than requested overflows the row cache.
- Extra results in reply to a FETCH, or to the queries of a keyset-driven cursor, are freed while still in use.
- A key query of a keyset-driven cursor answered with extra columns, or a re-read row with fewer columns, overflows the row cache.
- Replies without columns or rows, or with NULL values, to the driver's internal queries at connect time and in catalog functions are dereferenced.
- A malformed relacl value in SQLTablePrivileges() makes the driver write past a buffer.
- On Windows with MSDTC, a long transaction name returned by the server overflows a buffer during recovery.
- Values in replies to the driver's internal queries are used without checking their range: an empty column name, a parameter count, a large-object size, a function's or trigger's argument count, and a result of exactly 32767 columns. They are dereferenced, read past, returned to the application or sent back to the server as stack memory, or make the driver loop forever.
- A reply that ends a COPY, the connection or the transaction at an unexpected point leaves freed results, keysets or table information in use: a CopyOutResponse followed by a lost connection, a ROLLBACK command tag under UseDeclareFetch=1, or a lost connection while a cursor with positioned updates is closed. Eight extra bytes in a reply also make the driver wait forever for a COPY to end.
- On Windows, a start-up reply without client_encoding crashes the driver, and with MSDTC a failed connection makes the XA library use a connection it has already freed.
- An error message ending in the first byte of a multibyte character leaves the SQLSTATE returned by SQLGetDiagRecW() unterminated.
- When a string value did not fit the application's buffer, eight Unicode entry points filled the buffer and wrote no null terminator, so a caller that reads to the terminator, as ODBC allows, read past the end of its own buffer.

This continues the fixes for CVE-2026-120058 and CVE-2026-120060, which covered other replies. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction.
desc:
On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.
- The connections the driver opens itself ignored every libpq option given through pqopt, such as channel_binding=require, and the open string it registers with MSDTC carried no pqopt, so the XA library's connections dropped those options too.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: psqlODBC parsed and built connection strings in ways that let a value end early: - In a braced value, such as PWD={…}, a trailing byte 0x7d of a GBK, Big5 or SJIS character was…
desc:
psqlODBC parsed and built connection strings in ways that let a value end early:

- In a braced value, such as PWD={…}, a trailing byte 0x7d of a GBK, Big5 or SJIS character was taken for the closing brace.
- A braced value that ended right after an escaped }} was not reported as unterminated, and its contents were parsed as further keywords.
- SQLConnectW(), SQLDriverConnectW() and SQLBrowseConnectW() cut a connection string whose UTF-8 form is longer than 32767 bytes, which changes how the rest of it is parsed.
- On Windows with MSDTC, the password and user name were put into the XA open string without escaping, and the XA library copied each item of that string into a 64-byte stack buffer.
- Percent-encoding a long password wrote one byte past a 4096-byte stack buffer.

An end user who supplies a password, or another value the application puts into the connection string, can set other connection keywords, for example to connect the application to a server of their choosing. The MSDTC case can also overflow a stack buffer in the process that loads the XA library.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: psqlODBC builds queries of its own from names, and put these names into them without escaping or qualification: - the database name in SQLForeignKeys(); - the current schema name…
psqlODBC uses sizes and counts without checking their range, or keeps them in types too small for them: - A row array size of 0, set with SQLSetStmtAttr() or on the ARD, makes…
desc:
psqlODBC uses sizes and counts without checking their range, or keeps them in types too small for them:

- A row array size of 0, set with SQLSetStmtAttr() or on the ARD, makes SQLSetPos() with SQL_REFRESH write past the bound arrays.
- SQL_DESC_COUNT above 32767 on an APD or IPD writes before the start of a heap buffer.
- A numeric parameter with a negative scale overflows a stack buffer.
- SQLGetData() of a text value of 2 GiB or more into a wide-character buffer computes a wrapped size and overflows the heap.
- The 16-bit reference count and size of the statement parser's column-information cache wrap, which frees a cache entry still in use or overflows the cache, and a statement with more than 32768 columns overflows the parser's field array.
- An updatable cursor that records more than 65535 changes in one transaction wraps the 16-bit capacity of its rollback log, which overflows it and frees it twice.
- A statement with 32769 or more parameter markers overflows a 16-bit parameter count.
- A wide-character string of more than 2 GiB wraps the size of its UTF-8 conversion, which is then written below the start of a heap buffer.
- SQLGetDiagField() and SQLGetDiagFieldW() always stored the five-character SQLSTATE plus its terminator and checked BufferLength only afterwards, overrunning a buffer shorter than six bytes.
- The ANSI SQLSetDescField(SQL_DESC_NAME) on an IPD ignored BufferLength and copied the name with strdup(), reading a name passed as pointer plus length past its end.
- SQLFetchScroll(SQL_FETCH_BOOKMARK) did not check the bookmark it was given, so whoever chooses the bookmark value read out of bounds and crashed the process.
- Four places in the parameter conversion read one byte past the end of a bound character parameter, and one of them rewrote it.
- Binding a date, time or timestamp C value to an SQL_INTEGER or SQL_SMALLINT parameter dereferenced NULL instead of returning the conversion error.

Depending on the case, the values come from the application, from the data or statement text an end user supplies, or from a database user who controls the size of a table or value. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: With the driver's debug log (MyLog) turned on, two paths write the database password to the log in clear text, both beside a line where the driver's own redaction masks it as…
desc:
With the driver's debug log (MyLog) turned on, two paths write the database
password to the log in clear text, both beside a line where the driver's own
redaction masks it as PWD=xxxxx:

- Pressing "Test" in the Windows data source setup dialog (psqlsetup.dll)
  logs the whole connection string, which carries PWD= percent-encoded,
  which is reversible, and any password= or sslpassword= inside pqopt.
- The Unicode connect functions SQLDriverConnectW, SQLConnectW and
  SQLBrowseConnectW log their arguments as they convert them between UTF-16
  and UTF-8, before the masking happens. The ANSI entry points are unaffected.

Turning the log on takes an administrator, and MyLog is off by default. The
exposure is the person who later reads the log, which in practice means a log
attached to a bug report or handed to support. Making that safe is the purpose
of the driver's redaction, and these two sites bypassed it.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: psqlODBC frees memory that is still in use, frees it twice, or writes outside an application buffer in these cases: - The clean-up the driver runs at commit and rollback sends…
desc:
psqlODBC frees memory that is still in use, frees it twice, or writes outside an application buffer in these cases:

- The clean-up the driver runs at commit and rollback sends queries of its own, and the reply to one of them can start the clean-up again while it is running. The nested run frees the rollback log, or the list of cursors and prepared statements to close, and the outer run uses and frees it again.
- The callback through which libpq delivers notices could run that clean-up, and close the connection, while libpq was still using the connection.
- Freeing a statement whose result holds several cursors (FetchRefcursors=1, or UseDeclareFetch=1) used the freed first result while the later cursors were closed.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, after a rollback closed an updatable cursor, rows added or deleted through it were counted but not stored, so freeing the statement freed uninitialised pointers, and adding a row wrote past the keyset.
- After a multi-row fetch failed on a row other than the first of its rowset, SQLGetData() wrote at an offset past the buffer the application passed.
- SQLProcedureColumns() freed the result of its catalog query twice when the query failed.
- In a process named sqlservr (SQL Server linked servers), a server version below 8.4 made the statement parser free a buffer twice.
- A failed SQLPutData in the middle of a SQLSetPos() or SQLBulkOperations() data-at-execution sequence left the whole operation pending, with the internal statement still allocated and autocommit silently off, so later statements were rolled back at disconnect. The next positioned update ran the stale callback against a statement that was never executed and dereferenced NULL.

Most of these can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable). A database user who can make a statement fail, or who controls the contents of a row the application reads, can trigger the UseDeclareFetch=1 and SQLGetData() cases against an honest server. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: psqlODBC scans statement text itself to substitute parameters, translate ODBC escapes, join batched statements and rewrite queries for updatable cursors.
desc:
psqlODBC scans statement text itself to substitute parameters, translate ODBC escapes, join batched statements and rewrite queries for updatable cursors. Where it read the text differently from the server, text the driver took for data ran as SQL, or a positioned write went to another table:

- An escape string constant written e'…' in lower case was not recognised as one, and '…' after a keyword ending in E, as in LIKE'…', was taken for one.
- A } inside a quoted literal ended an ODBC {d …}, {t …}, {ts …} or {escape …} sequence.
- Dollar-quote tags containing _ were not recognised, and an identifier starting with _ followed by $, such as _$$, was taken for the start of a dollar quote, so a parameter marker inside a literal was substituted.
- A trailing -- comment in one statement of a batched parameter array swallowed the next statement.
- Comments, literals longer than 255 bytes and escape strings were misread when the driver located the FROM and WHERE clauses of a query for an updatable cursor, and the text copied into the cursor's own queries could include SQL from inside a literal.
- A table name containing $ was cut at the $, and a quoted table name starting with , or ; ended the table list, so positioned updates, inserts and deletes went to another table.
- An integer parameter with an embedded NUL byte cut the query short.
- /*/ was taken for a comment that opens and closes, while the server reads it as one that only opens.
- ConnSettings was split at every semicolon, including one inside a quoted literal, so an application that puts an end user's value into a SET command there ran the rest of the value as SQL at connect time.

An end user who controls text the application puts into a statement, or a parameter value, can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. A database user who can create a table with a crafted name can redirect another user's positioned writes to a table of their choosing.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: To build positioned updates and to describe columns, psqlODBC matches the names in a statement against the catalog.
desc:
To build positioned updates and to describe columns, psqlODBC matches the names in a statement against the catalog. Where it matched differently from the server, it used another table or column:

- Table and schema names were compared case-insensitively in its column-information cache, so users could be taken for another user's "Users", and the driver then evaluated that table's column default to answer @@IDENTITY.
- In FROM ONLY t, ONLY was taken for the table name.
- Column names were compared case-insensitively, so with Parse=1 the type of another column could decide the size of the application's buffer, which a fetch then overflowed.
- In a database whose encoding is single-byte, such as LATIN1 or SQL_ASCII, the server folds the accented letters of an unquoted name by its own locale, while the driver folded only A-Z, so ÉTAT could be taken for another user's "État" instead of état.
- On systems other than Windows, in a Turkish or Azeri locale, an unquoted I was not folded to i, and keywords and ODBC function names did not match.
- Without a schema name, SQLSpecialColumns() could report the key columns of another user's same-named temporary table, and SQLPrimaryKeys() could take another user's index named <table>_pkey for the primary key of a table without one.
- After search_path changed other than through a plain SET statement, positioned writes went to the same-named table in the previously current schema.
- SQLBulkOperations() trusted the ctid stored inside a variable-length bookmark handed back by the application, and ignored the WHERE clause that restricted the cursor, so a forged bookmark read, updated or deleted any row of the cursor's table.

A database user who can create a table in a schema on another user's search_path can redirect that user's positioned updates, inserts and deletes to a table of their choosing, where they run with the victim's rights, or run an expression of their choosing under the victim's role.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends.
desc:
To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends. It treated a client encoding named by an alias the server accepts, such as WIN950, Windows950 or big-5 for BIG5, as single-byte, and it accepted too narrow a range of lead bytes for JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR. A quote byte that the server reads as part of such a character was then not doubled, or a quote the server reads on its own was taken for part of a character, and the literal ended early.

An end user who controls one bound character parameter, or a name the application passes to a catalog function such as SQLTables(), can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. This requires a connection that is not in UTF-8: the ANSI driver, or the ANSI entry points, with one of these client encodings. For bound parameters the driver must also be substituting parameters itself, as it does with UseServerSidePrepare=0 or a cursor type other than forward-only.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: psqlODBC read memory it had not written, or memory past the end of an application buffer, and sent it to the server or returned it to the application: - Text bound as SQL_C_CHAR…
desc:
psqlODBC read memory it had not written, or memory past the end of an application buffer, and sent it to the server or returned it to the application:

- Text bound as SQL_C_CHAR to a large-object parameter was read past the end of the application's buffer, and the extra bytes were stored in the large object.
- After a fetch truncated a long bytea or large-object value, positioned updates and inserts read past the bound buffer and wrote that memory into the row.
- Hex text with a NUL byte, bound to a binary parameter with an explicit length, sent uninitialised heap memory as the parameter value.
- With RowVersioning=1, SQLColumns() on a table that does not exist returned uninitialised stack memory as the schema and table names.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, bookmarks of updatable block cursors contained uninitialised heap memory, and a malformed ctid from the server sent stale heap bytes in positioned updates and deletes.
- With UseServerSidePrepare=0, calling SQLNumResultCols(), SQLDescribeCol() or SQLColAttribute() on a prepared statement before SQLExecute() read the application's bound parameter buffers and sent their current contents to the server as literals, although ODBC lets the application fill those buffers after the describe.
- The driver named the prepared statements, savepoints, cursors and keyset plans it creates on the server after the heap addresses of its own objects, so the server, or anyone reading an unencrypted connection, learned exact heap addresses inside the client.

Depending on the case, an end user who supplies a parameter value, a database user who stores a long value in a row, or a hostile server can obtain memory of the application process, which may hold data of other users or credentials.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

title: A flaw was found in the Keycloak Operator.
desc: A flaw was found in the Keycloak Operator. Deterministic hashes derived from Kubernetes Secrets are published in generated StatefulSet metadata and in KeycloakOIDCClient status. A user with read access to those resources may be able to recover a low-entropy credential referenced by a Secret, even when Kubernetes RBAC denies the user access to the Secret itself.

title: A vulnerability was identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af.
desc: A vulnerability was identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af. Affected by this vulnerability is the function Uploads::saveFile/Auth::init of the file src/Uploads.php of the component Authorization Subsystem. Such manipulation of the argument PicoContentEditorUpload leads to unrestricted upload. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

title: A vulnerability was found in browser-use 0.13.13/0.13.14.
desc: A vulnerability was found in browser-use 0.13.13/0.13.14. This impacts the function load_and_migrate_config of the file browser_use/config.py of the component SecurityWatchdog. The manipulation results in improper authorization. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

title: A vulnerability has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1.
desc: A vulnerability has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. This affects the function update of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. The manipulation leads to dynamically-determined object attributes. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The identifier of the patch is 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

title: A flaw has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1.
desc: A flaw has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The impacted element is the function store of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. Executing a manipulation can lead to dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. This patch is called 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.

title: A vulnerability was detected in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1.
desc: A vulnerability was detected in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The affected element is the function Store/Update of the file modules/User/Http/Controllers/UserController.php of the component User Management. Performing a manipulation results in dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The patch is named 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.

title: A flaw was found in the file-gif-load plugin in GIMP.
desc: A flaw was found in the file-gif-load plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted JIF image file, a 32-bit integer overflow occurs during the pixel buffer size calculation, while the zlib output limit is computed separately without wrapping. This leads to an undersized heap allocation, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow when the compressed image data is decompressed. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

AWS has addressed this issue. No customer action is required.

The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Affected by this vulnerability is the function _load_index of the file src/vanna/integrations/faiss/agent_memory.py of the component FAISS AgentMemory Integration. Performing a manipulation results in deserialization. The attack needs to be approached locally. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

title: A vulnerability was identified in Backdrop CMS up to 1.35.2.
desc: A vulnerability was identified in Backdrop CMS up to 1.35.2. Affected is the function get_argument of the file core/modules/views/plugins/views_plugin_argument_default_php.inc of the component Views Module. Such manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The config-import path enforces no 'use PHP for settings' check while the Views PHP-code argument plugin executes eval() without a permission check, confirming the authorization bypass. The vendor explains: "As per our security advisory policy, no security advisory is required when an exploit requires 'advanced permissions'."

Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. Patch name: 0fdff6ed12b58ad4c33aab5a63f66e04555cafb6. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files readable by the Package Manager service account via a filesystem path appended to the request URI in Posit Software, PBC Posit Package Manager: 





  *  before 2025.09.6,
  *  2025.12.x before 2025.12.4
  *  2026.04.x before 2026.04.4
  *  2026.05.x before 2026.05.2
  *  2026.06.x before 2026.06.2
  *  2026.08.x before 2026.08.2
  *  2026.09.x before 2026.09.2
  *  2026.10.x before 2026.10.2
  *  2026.11.x before 2026.11.2








NOTE: In the default configuration, where Server.LandingPage is unset, request paths are resolved from the filesystem root, so no directory-traversal sequences are required and exploitation is not detected by scanners that test only for ../ sequences.

title: The fix for CVE-2026-61801 added file type and size checks when parsing user and group files in github.com/moby/sys/user, but did not apply them consistently across all parsing…
desc: The fix for CVE-2026-61801 added file type and size checks when parsing user and group files in github.com/moby/sys/user, but did not apply them consistently across all parsing and lookup functions. ParsePasswdFile, ParsePasswdFileFilter, GetAdditionalGroupsPath, ParseSubIDFile, ParseSubIDFileFilter, ParseIDMapFile, ParseIDMapFileFilter, LookupUser, LookupUid, LookupGroup and LookupGid could still read large or unbounded files. An attacker who controls the contents of a user or group file processed by an affected application, such as /etc/passwd or /etc/group from a container image, can cause excessive memory or CPU consumption, resulting in a denial of service. Exploitation depends on how the consuming application uses the affected functions. Fixed in v0.5.1 by enforcing the 10 MiB read limit in all affected functions. Docker Engine 29.10.1 includes the fix.

title: A vulnerability was identified in Dispatcharr up to 0.32.0.
desc: A vulnerability was identified in Dispatcharr up to 0.32.0. Affected by this issue is the function get_permissions of the component VODLogoViewSet/M3UAccountViewSet. Such manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack may be launched remotely. Upgrading to version 0.33.0 can resolve this issue. The name of the patch is ac7a23cc584761b88f8d87dd8ac3688426024ed8. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

title: A vulnerability was determined in beenuar AiSOC up to 17.0.0.
desc: A vulnerability was determined in beenuar AiSOC up to 17.0.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the component AuditMiddleware. This manipulation causes improper verification of cryptographic signature. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 17.1.0 addresses this issue. Patch name: 8f2224299124010536ff0e3ebcd9efb0149af26c. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

title: A flaw has been found in GouguCMS up to 4.08.18.
desc: A flaw has been found in GouguCMS up to 4.08.18. This affects the function detail of the file app/home/controller/Pages.php. Executing a manipulation can lead to code injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

title: A vulnerability was found in zhblue hustoj up to 26.08.19.
desc: A vulnerability was found in zhblue hustoj up to 26.08.19. Affected is the function prepare_files of the file trunk/core/judge_client/judge_client.cc. The manipulation results in os command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 26.10.31 is able to address this issue. The patch is identified as 07c73e1434c4c8e49094396c7d93bb09d6f159a4. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

title: A vulnerability has been found in zhblue hustoj up to 26.08.19.
desc: A vulnerability has been found in zhblue hustoj up to 26.08.19. This impacts an unknown function of the file trunk/core/judged/judged.cc of the component Judge Daemon Sandbox. The manipulation leads to execution with unnecessary privileges. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Upgrading to version 26.10.31 will fix this issue. The identifier of the patch is 07c73e1434c4c8e49094396c7d93bb09d6f159a4/b5488154c7842fbfa0c38af93a737a85622cdf86. The affected component should be upgraded.

title: A flaw was found in Red Hat Enterprise Linux's qemu-kvm virtualization software.
desc: A flaw was found in Red Hat Enterprise Linux's qemu-kvm virtualization software. A privileged user inside a guest virtual machine could use this flaw to make the host QEMU process copy parts of its own memory into the guest's memory, where the attacker could read it. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to view portions of the host QEMU process memory from within a guest, potentially exposing sensitive information that could aid in further attacks. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality.

title: A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used for managing authentication and authorization flows.
desc: A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used for managing authentication and authorization flows. The issue occurs when a client policy is configured to enforce a high-assurance authentication flow requiring OTP. Due to improper validation of existing sessions, a lower-assurance password-only SSO session can be incorrectly accepted if the request does not explicitly demand a specific assurance level. This allows an attacker with access to a user's password or session to bypass the second factor and obtain tokens claiming a higher level of security.

title: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could…
desc: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to send requests to internal network resources due to insufficient validation in repository import.

title: Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-15 contained a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to store markup in the profile full_name field by…
desc: Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-15 contained a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to store markup in the profile full_name field by submitting a modified request directly to the backend, which persists the value without sanitization. The Contact Support workflow later inserts the stored name into the generated support email without HTML encoding, so attackers can make injected HTML and media, such as misleading banners, masked hyperlinks and external tracking resources, render in support messages received by the support team.

title: Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-07 contained a broken object level authorization vulnerability in the PUT /api/invoice/{invoice_id}/extracted-data endpoint, which accepts a…
desc: Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-07 contained a broken object level authorization vulnerability in the PUT /api/invoice/{invoice_id}/extracted-data endpoint, which accepts a client-supplied extracted_data object without verifying invoice ownership, enforcing the invoice_edit permission or checking whether the invoice has been soft deleted. Authenticated attackers who know an invoice identifier can overwrite seller and buyer details, invoice identifiers, product entries, totals and custom metadata of invoices, including archived invoices marked is_deleted = 1, undermining the integrity of financial records.

title: Author Avatars List/Block plugin for WordPress before 2.2.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access…
desc: Author Avatars List/Block plugin for WordPress before 2.2.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to inject arbitrary JavaScript via the card_min_width, card_max_width, card_min_height, and card_max_height attributes of the [authoravatars] shortcode. Attackers can supply a value containing a double quote to break out of the card's style attribute and add event handlers, causing the injected script to execute in the browser of any visitor, including editors or administrators who view the rendered user card.

title: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management.
desc: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.11, singleton-scoped ExportService stores the per-request identifiers this.idCsv and this.idZip as BehaviorSubjects and keeps derived directory names in instance fields, while singleton-scoped ImportService stores per-request paths in this._dirname and this._extractPath. Concurrent requests by different tenant administrators to /export, /export/template, /export/filter, or /import can interleave while asynchronous file operations are in progress, allowing one tenant's export archive to be delivered, overwritten, or deleted by another operation, or causing one tenant's import to read another tenant's uploaded CSV data and persist it under the wrong tenant. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.11.

title: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management.
desc: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.44.2, getTracker in packages/core/src/lib/throttler/throttler-behind-proxy.guard.ts accepts CF-Connecting-IP without verifying that a trusted Cloudflare edge supplied it; when CF-Connecting-IP is absent, app.set('trust proxy', true) can let an attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-For value determine req.ip. In deployments where a trusted intermediary does not overwrite these headers, or where the firewall permits direct API access, varying the applicable header on repeated POST /auth/login requests gives an unauthenticated remote attacker a distinct throttle bucket for each attempt, so the five-attempts-per-60-seconds limit does not trigger and no account lockout, CAPTCHA, or exponential backoff limits password guessing. This issue is fixed in version 111.44.2.

title: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management.
desc: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.13, POST /api/integration/github/webhook in packages/plugins/integration-github/src/lib/probot/probot.discovery.ts passes request bodies through ProbotDiscovery.receiveHook to probot.receive without verifying x-hub-signature-256 against the configured webhook secret. Because the route is public and uses the attacker-controlled installation.id to locate integrations, an unauthenticated remote attacker who knows or guesses an installation identifier can forge installation deletion events that remove a tenant's GitHub integration or forge issues events that insert fabricated issue data into the tenant's automation pipeline. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.13.

title: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management.
desc: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.9, OrganizationPermissionGuard in packages/core/src/lib/shared/guards/organization-permission.guard.ts checks allowManualTime, allowModifyTime, and allowDeleteTime only when the caller's role is EMPLOYEE and unconditionally authorizes other roles. A tenant administrator who grants ALLOW_MANUAL_TIME, ALLOW_MODIFY_TIME, or ALLOW_DELETE_TIME to MANAGER, DATA_ENTRY, VIEWER, or another non-employee role can therefore leave the organization-wide policy disabled while that role still creates, modifies, or deletes time records, undermining payroll and billing integrity. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.9.

title: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management.
desc: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.44.3, per-request JWT validation in packages/core/src/lib/auth/strategies/jwt.strategy.ts accepts the result of UserService.getIfExists in packages/core/src/lib/user/user.service.ts without requiring User.isActive to be true and User.isArchived to be false. When a token contains an organizationId claim, the active and archived status check applies to the UserOrganization record rather than the User entity. After an administrator deactivates an account through PATCH /api/user/:id, an existing access token can continue to authenticate API requests at the account's previous privilege level until expiration, up to 24 hours by default. This issue is fixed in version 111.44.3.

title: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management.
desc: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.10, RoleGuard authorizes requests using the role claim embedded in an access token instead of the user's current database role in packages/core/src/lib/core/context/request-context.ts through RequestContext.hasRoles. After an administrator demotes a user, an already-issued token can continue to pass role checks for up to the token's 24-hour default lifetime, including on DELETE /api/tenant and other RolesEnum.SUPER_ADMIN or ADMIN guarded routes, which can preserve tenant-destructive and billing privileges after revocation. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.10.

title: A flaw was found in kubevirt Containerized Data Importer (CDI).
desc: A flaw was found in kubevirt Containerized Data Importer (CDI). The CDI clone controller derives the CommonName of a CDI-CA-signed upload client certificate from the tenant-settable cdi.kubevirt.io/uploadClientName PVC annotation without validation, and the upload server authenticates clients only by certificate CA chain and CommonName string match, with no namespace or PVC binding. A namespace user can obtain a valid client certificate and write arbitrary data into any upload-ready PVC in any namespace whose upload Service is reachable from the cluster network, resulting in cross-namespace integrity impact on disk images used by virtual machines.

title: A vulnerability in the MongoDB integration package for the Laravel framework allows an unauthorized user to bypass mass assignment attribute protections.
desc: A vulnerability in the MongoDB integration package for the Laravel framework allows an unauthorized user to bypass mass assignment attribute protections. When an application uses attribute deny-lists to guard sensitive model fields, specially crafted request payloads containing database operator keys can circumvent these protections. An unauthorized user with network access to an affected application endpoint can modify guarded attributes, potentially leading to privilege escalation within the application

title: An improper restriction of dynamically determined object attributes in the object-document mapping library's association handling allows structured input supplied in place of a…
desc: An improper restriction of dynamically determined object attributes in the object-document mapping library's association handling allows structured input supplied in place of a simple identifier value to be turned into an object that is treated as an already-stored record of a caller-chosen model class. In applications that pass unfiltered request data into the affected association handling, an unauthenticated party may cause unintended modification or removal of stored records, and may render an individual record unreadable through that association.

title: A type-confusion weakness in the Extended JSON parsing component of BSON for Ruby allows a party who can supply parser input to influence how a serialized document is framed.
desc: A type-confusion weakness in the Extended JSON parsing component of BSON for Ruby allows a party who can supply parser input to influence how a serialized document is framed. Content placed in one value may be read back as additional or replacement document fields. An unauthenticated party supplying input to an application that parses untrusted Extended JSON and stores the result may cause unintended modification of stored data.

title: An information exposure weakness in the connection string handling of the MongoDB Ruby Driver can place credential material from the application's own configuration into the text…
desc: An information exposure weakness in the connection string handling of the MongoDB Ruby Driver can place credential material from the application's own configuration into the text of a parsing error, where an existing redaction control does not apply. A party able to read the application's error output or logs may thereby obtain database credential text together with deployment coordinates. The condition arises entirely within the embedding application process and requires no database authentication.

title: The MongoDB C Driver does not confirm that the party signing a supplied certificate revocation status response is authorized to answer for the certificate being checked.
desc: The MongoDB C Driver does not confirm that the party signing a supplied certificate revocation status response is authorized to answer for the certificate being checked. An unauthenticated party that operates the TLS endpoint a client connects to can therefore have a withdrawn certificate accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of the application's database traffic and in the loss of the revocation decision.

title: An improper handling of repeated fields in encryption key documents in the MongoDB encryption support library may allow memory to be retained without release.
desc: An improper handling of repeated fields in encryption key documents in the MongoDB encryption support library may allow memory to be retained without release. A party able to write to the key storage collection, or a database endpoint returning such a document, may cause the memory use of the calling application process to grow for each document parsed, which may reduce performance of that process.

title: MongoDB C Driver contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the credential-selection logic used by its AWS authentication mechanism.
desc: MongoDB C Driver contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the credential-selection logic used by its AWS authentication mechanism. A process-wide credential cache can take precedence over the credentials supplied for an individual connection, so a connection configured with one set of credentials may instead be authenticated under an identity cached earlier in the same process. A party able to cause the application process to open an additional connection may thereby obtain unintended privileges.

title: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.10 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have…
desc: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.10 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to perform server-side request forgery against internal network resources due to insufficient URL validation in MCP server OAuth handling.

title: In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.9, the nginx reverse proxy configurations shipped with Ditto (Helm chart, Docker Compose, Kubernetes and OpenShift deployment files)…
desc:
In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.9, the nginx reverse proxy configurations shipped with Ditto (Helm chart, Docker Compose, Kubernetes and OpenShift deployment files) forward a client-supplied

  `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` header to the Ditto gateway on locations that do not apply nginx authentication, such as `/api/2/connections`. nginx selects the location based on the normalized request URI
  but forwards the raw URI, while the gateway does not treat an encoded slash (`%2f`) as a path separator. A crafted request path is therefore routed by nginx through such an unauthenticated location and
  by the gateway to the regular Things and Policies HTTP API, including routes that send live messages to devices. When pre-authentication is enabled (the default of the Helm chart and the Docker Compose
  setup), an unauthenticated remote attacker can impersonate arbitrary policy subjects and read, modify and delete Things, read Policies, send messages to devices and create entities. Additionally, the
  optional Ingress of the Helm chart (Ditto 3.9.0 to 3.9.9) routes requests directly to the gateway without setting or removing that header, and the WebSocket Ingress of the Helm chart of Ditto 3.3.0 to
  3.8.15 does not set it, allowing the same impersonation without path manipulation when pre-authentication is enabled. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-120753.

title: A data-query neutralization weakness in the query builder of the MongoDB integration for a PHP web framework allows values supplied to certain bulk counter-update helpers to be…
desc: A data-query neutralization weakness in the query builder of the MongoDB integration for a PHP web framework allows values supplied to certain bulk counter-update helpers to be interpreted by the database as query expressions rather than stored as plain text. An application that passes externally supplied data into these helpers may write unintended values into stored documents and may result in unintended disclosure of other data held on the same document. No credentials are required of the party supplying the value.

title: An improper certificate revocation check in the MongoDB Python Driver's optional TLS revocation-checking support allows an unauthenticated party that operates the network…
desc: An improper certificate revocation check in the MongoDB Python Driver's optional TLS revocation-checking support allows an unauthenticated party that operates the network endpoint a client connects to, and that holds a revoked but still-dated certificate trusted by that client, to have the connection accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of application credentials and other session data, and in the client treating responses from that endpoint as genuine.

title: A polymorphic relationship query helper in the MongoDB Eloquent integration for Laravel resolves a record's type identifier inconsistently between the code that stores a…
desc: A polymorphic relationship query helper in the MongoDB Eloquent integration for Laravel resolves a record's type identifier inconsistently between the code that stores a relationship link and the code that searches for one. An application that relies on a relationship-absence query to restrict which records a request may see or change can therefore have that restriction silently fail, allowing a user with basic application privileges to read and to modify or remove records the restriction was meant to cover.

title: A query builder component in a MongoDB integration library for a PHP web framework does not run the query-modification callbacks that an application registers with the framework…
desc: A query builder component in a MongoDB integration library for a PHP web framework does not run the query-modification callbacks that an application registers with the framework before sending read, update, and delete operations to the database. As a result, a filter that an application relies on to limit which records a request may touch can be omitted silently. A user with basic application privileges may be able to read or change records that the application intended to keep out of reach.

title: An incorrect authorization weakness in the embedded relation handling of the Laravel MongoDB library may allow a user with basic application privileges to alter records belonging…
desc: An incorrect authorization weakness in the embedded relation handling of the Laravel MongoDB library may allow a user with basic application privileges to alter records belonging to other users. After an embedded relation is pre-loaded, a routine write on that record is issued without the constraint that limits it to the record the user is permitted to change. This may result in unintended modification or loss of stored data for other users of the same application.

title: A logic flaw in the query-building layer of the Mongoid object-document mapper causes a model-level default restriction that is meant to return no records to be silently…
desc: A logic flaw in the query-building layer of the Mongoid object-document mapper causes a model-level default restriction that is meant to return no records to be silently discarded when it is combined into a query. A user with basic application privileges who sends an ordinary request may read, change, or remove records that the restriction was intended to withhold.

title: Mongoid may omit a field from the client-side encryption settings it generates for a collection when that same field is also used as a reference to another record.
desc: Mongoid may omit a field from the client-side encryption settings it generates for a collection when that same field is also used as a reference to another record. The value is then stored in readable form instead of encrypted, and the application receives no indication that this has happened. A party with ordinary authenticated read access to the affected collection may be able to view data that was intended to be protected.

title: Mongoid contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the handling of caller-supplied filters for bulk removal through a referenced association.
desc: Mongoid contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the handling of caller-supplied filters for bulk removal through a referenced association. Conditions already attached to the association can take precedence over the filter the caller supplied, so records the caller did not select may be removed. A user with basic privileges in an application built on the library may cause unintended removal of records belonging to the same parent record.

title: Mongoid does not consistently apply its read-only attribute protection when attribute names are supplied dynamically by the caller.
desc: Mongoid does not consistently apply its read-only attribute protection when attribute names are supplied dynamically by the caller. In an application that forwards caller-supplied attribute names into a document update, a user with basic application privileges may change values held inside a field the model declared immutable. This may result in unintended modification of data the application treats as trusted, such as flags used for its own access decisions.

title: Mongoid builds an incomplete automatic encryption schema for certain embedded document associations.
desc: Mongoid builds an incomplete automatic encryption schema for certain embedded document associations. As a result, values that the application declared as encrypted may be written to the database in cleartext, with no error or warning returned to the application. A party holding only basic read privileges on the affected collection, and no access to the encryption keys, may then obtain those values in readable form.

title: A NULL pointer dereference and invalid memory release in the server discovery component of the MongoDB C Driver may allow an unauthenticated party that controls a server…
desc: A NULL pointer dereference and invalid memory release in the server discovery component of the MongoDB C Driver may allow an unauthenticated party that controls a server endpoint, or that can alter unencrypted network traffic, to cause a client application to terminate by sending a crafted discovery response.

title: An invalid memory release in the MongoDB PHP Driver extension occurs when certain string-typed options or type-mapping settings are given non-string values.
desc: An invalid memory release in the MongoDB PHP Driver extension occurs when certain string-typed options or type-mapping settings are given non-string values. A party who can run PHP code in a process that loads the extension may corrupt process memory. This can lead to reading or changing process memory, running commands as the PHP process user, or crashing the process.

title: A race condition during docker cp mount setup in Docker Engine allows a malicious container to leave a read-only bind mount writable while an archive is extracted into the…
desc: A race condition during docker cp mount setup in Docker Engine allows a malicious container to leave a read-only bind mount writable while an archive is extracted into the container. When copying files into a container, the daemon bind-mounts the container's volumes into a temporary view and applies the read-only flags afterwards, through a path inside the container's filesystem. A process in the container can change that path in between, so the flags are applied to a different mount and the intended bind mount stays writable for the duration of the copy.

title: An unencrypted RSA private key for a default HTTPS certificate is included in GeoVision GV-EBD4700 firmware V1.11 (A02-GV-EBD4700_V1.11_2026_10_13.zip) at…
desc:
An unencrypted RSA private key for a default HTTPS certificate is included in GeoVision GV-EBD4700 firmware V1.11 (A02-GV-EBD4700_V1.11_2026_10_13.zip) at /program/www/ssl_cert.pem and copied to /config/ssl_cert.pem during initialization. When HTTPS is enabled using the default certificate, a network on-path attacker who obtains the firmware image can use the exposed private key to present an identical certificate and intercept HTTPS traffic. HTTPS is disabled by default .


  *  

Only impacts deployments where an administrator enables HTTPS and retains the default certificate. Because the private key is publicly distributed in the firmware image, an on-path attacker can impersonate the device with an identical certificate fingerprint, bypassing fingerprint checks and stored certificate exceptions (potentially capturing credentials if a user clicks through the expired-certificate warning).

title: When the proxy option isn't set, HttpClient takes the proxy from environment variables like http_proxy or HTTP_PROXY.
desc:
When the proxy option isn't set, HttpClient takes the proxy from environment variables like http_proxy or HTTP_PROXY. On web servers, it ignores HTTP_PROXY, because PHP puts the Proxy request header there (the httpoxy issue). On the CLI SAPI, it read HTTP_PROXY from $_SERVER, where PHP also puts the environment.

HTTP workers that run under the CLI SAPI put the headers of each request in $_SERVER too. This is the case of spiral/roadrunner-http, which the RoadRunner runner of php-runtime uses, and of baldinof/roadrunner-bundle and php-pm. A client could then send a Proxy header to choose the proxy of the requests that the application sent while handling its request. That proxy received the full requests to http:// URLs, with their credentials, and could forge the responses. For https:// URLs, it learned the host and port through CONNECT.

NativeHttpClient is affected since Symfony 4.3.0, AmpHttpClient since 5.1.0, and CurlHttpClient since 4.4.40, 5.4.7 and 6.0.7.

On the CLI SAPI, HTTP_PROXY is now read from the environment with $_ENV and getenv(), never from $_SERVER. Other SAPIs still ignore it.

title: Since Symfony 7.2, expressions can contain comments.
desc:
Since Symfony 7.2, expressions can contain comments. The lexer used a regular expression to find the end of a comment. When a /* was never closed, this regular expression scanned the rest of the expression, and the lexer then went on with the next character. So each /* scanned the rest of the expression again. Linting 192 KB of /*  took 9 to 11 seconds, and 96 KB took 34 seconds without PCRE JIT.

The lexer runs before the parser and its nesting limit. Any code that lints or parses untrusted expressions is affected, including the ExpressionSyntax validation constraint. A Length constraint on the same value doesn't help, since the validator runs both constraints.

The lexer now uses strpos() to find the end of a comment, and a comment that is never closed throws a SyntaxError. Such expressions were already invalid. Lexing takes linear time again.

title: The fix for CVE-2017-16652 restricts the redirects of HttpUtils::createRedirectResponse() to the host of the request.
desc:
The fix for CVE-2017-16652 restricts the redirects of HttpUtils::createRedirectResponse() to the host of the request. When framework.session.cookie_domain is set, it also allows the subdomains of that domain. To check a target, it read the host of the URL up to the first "/". But browsers also end the host at "\", "?" and "#". So with the cookie domain .example.com, a target like https://evil.test?.example.com passed the check, and the browser went to evil.test.

Applications are exposed when framework.session.cookie_domain is set. The default success and failure handlers of form_login redirect to the _target_path or _failure_path of the request. A login link can then send the user to another site right after a successful login, for example to ask for the password again.

HttpUtils now ends the host of a target where browsers do, before checking it against the allowed domains.

title: Improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an…
desc:
Improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to run the runbook to set unintended configuration in the account's Regional Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) via a crafted S3KeyPrefix parameter value. This applies only when that document does not already exist in the Region. The unintended configuration can include arbitrary commands, which then run on managed instances when other users start Session Manager sessions.



Because any user permitted to run the runbook selects which revision to run, this issue remains reachable in an affected Region until earlier revisions can no longer be run there. AWS is deprecating all revisions created before 2026-10-22 (UTC) in every Region and partition beginning January 15, 2027; until deprecation, earlier revisions remain runnable, so upgrading alone is not sufficient.



To remediate this issue:



1. Run the latest revision of the runbook. The latest revision is the fixed revision in every Region where the runbook is available, and its revision number varies by Region. To find it, run aws ssm describe-document --name AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 --region <region> --query "Document.LatestVersion". Update any Automation executions, State Manager associations, AWS Config remediation configurations, or other automations pinned to an earlier revision to use the latest revision. 2. Until earlier revisions are removed in your Region, either keep untrusted users from running earlier revisions of the runbook, or keep a trusted Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in every Region. Earlier revisions inject only when they create this document, so while a trusted one exists, this path is closed in that Region. 3. Review your Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in any Region where it was first created by an earlier revision of this runbook, not by you. To check, look for any run of this runbook that failed with "DOCUMENT CREATE OR UPDATE FAILED." An injected run always fails with this error. You can also compare the creation date of the document's first version with the start times of runs of this runbook in that Region. Check the document for settings you did not configure, especially shellProfile, Run As (runAsEnabled, runAsDefaultUser), maxSessionDuration, idleSessionTimeout, and the logging destination fields. The fixed runbook updates only the S3 bucket and prefix fields of an existing preferences document, so settings injected earlier remain until you remove them. If you find unexpected settings, restore your trusted preferences and review instances on which Session Manager sessions were started while those settings were active. The AWS Security Bulletin includes commands for this review.
